question: Which of the following conversions are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __1 L = 1 dm3 **(and 1 mL = 1 cm3)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 1 L = 1 dm3__ is a standard conversion in the metric system.
 
• 1 mL is equivalent to 1 cm3 or one cubic centimeter.
 
• The conversion ensures consistency in measuring liquid volumes and spatial capacities.
 
• These conversions are widely used in scientific, industrial, and everyday contexts.
 
• The metric system simplifies calculations by using powers of 10 for all conversions.
 
• The statement 1 L = 1000 dm3 or 1 mL = 1000 cm3 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Metric System Conversions:**
 
 
• 1 liter (L) = 1000 milliliters (mL).
 
• 1 milliliter (mL) = 1 cubic centimeter (cm3).
 
• 1 cubic meter (m3) = 1000 liters (L).
 
 
 
• **Importance in Science and Engineering:**
 
 
• These conversions are critical in fields such as chemistry, physics, and engineering.
 
• They ensure precise measurements and compatibility across different systems of units.
